newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude and gas oil weaker, supports hold.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude and gas oil weaker, supports hold.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures opened weaker, but traders said there was little conviction to the downside with trading volume thin.
By 0930 GMT September gas oil stood $1.50 lower at $169.75 after slipping through technical trendline support around $170 but failing to break down further support around $169-$169.50 a tonne.
The October Brent contract was 12 cents down at $18.87 a barrel, holding above initial support at $18.80 a barrel.
"Global demand is fairly supportive at the moment, even though Iraqi oil will eventually have its effect on prices," Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said in his daily report.
"U.S. refiner demand is good, helped by a cutback in Canadian shipments for September, while the North Sea is influenced by the lower September loading programmes," he added.

From a technical point of view, because the supports continue to hold, most analysts see the overall trend staying higher in the longer term, but with momentum indicators in neutral, the pace of the rise may be slow and there may be a further period of consolidation today.
"The market is in a slow but steady bullish uptrend channel very clearly seen on the weekly chart," said Tom James, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore.

James pegged the technical trading range for this week in the $18.42 to $19.48 region with a break of either of these significant for the market trend, in particular the $18.42 level which represents weekly trendline support that was broken briefly last week.
